subjects.name: Winter solstice revelry and Christmas traditions

summary: A history of midwinter revelry from Roman Saturnalia and Germanic Yule to medieval English Christmas, and of the Church's and the Puritans' long, largely failed attempts to suppress it, ending with the 1640s-1650s Christmas bans.
keywords: Cool People Who Did Cool Stuff

evidence.note: Host frames the story as a centuries-long church war against riotous solstice festivities
St. Lucy's Day, its Scandinavian popularity and the Syracuse martyr legend
Long segment on Roman Saturnalia: role reversal, Lord of Saturnalia, sacrifice
Yule segment: Odin, Yule log, trees, Wild Hunt
Finnish Christmas goat figure discussed as a Santa source
Eighth-century bishop's complaint about pagan-style street revelry
Lord of Misrule in medieval England
Church condemnations of animal masquerade and ritual cross-dressing across centuries
English Civil War context: Puritan parliament turns Christmas into a culture war
Canterbury plum pudding riots against the Christmas ban
Soviet ban and rebranding of Christmas as New Year; short coda

notes: Cool People Who Did Cool Stuff crossover; hero chosen over crossover per precedence, as the revelers are framed as the cool people. Survey of a practice, so spans are rough: start uses the traditional Saturnalia reform date (217 BCE) and main_span runs from the first recorded Dec 25 Christmas (336) to the Restoration (1660). Soviet ban and modern drag-show attacks are brief and left out. No theme fits festivals, paganism or LGBTQ history.
